537	// rebuildCheckpointCommit re-parents the commit onto parent (backend-agnostic:
538	// the v1 chain passes the rewritten predecessor, a standalone checkpoint ref
539	// passes the commit's own original parent). Already-applied
540	// commits keep their tree (idempotent); unapplied commits get a tree
541	// rebuilt from redactedByPath (precomputed by the orchestrator's single
542	// OPF batch call) plus an Entire-OPF-Applied: true trailer.
543	//
544	// redactedByPath maps each redactable blob's full tree path (e.g.
545	// "ab/cd.../0/full.jsonl") to its OPF-redacted bytes. Only required for
546	// unapplied commits; pass nil for already-applied ones.
547	//
548	// Correctness note: each v1 commit tree is cumulative. During a multi-commit
549	// rewrite, the newest original commit can still contain older shards that were
550	// regex-only before this rewrite. The collect/apply walkers redact the whole
551	// tree for every unapplied commit so the final rewritten tip cannot
552	// reintroduce an older un-OPF-redacted shard.
553	func rebuildCheckpointCommit(ctx context.Context, repo *git.Repository, oldCommit *object.Commit, parent plumbing.Hash, redactedByPath map[string][]byte) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
554		newTree := oldCommit.TreeHash
555		if !trailers.HasOPFApplied(oldCommit.Message) {
556			tree, err := repo.TreeObject(oldCommit.TreeHash)
557			if err != nil {
558				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load tree: %w", err)
559			}
560			// Whole-tree redaction — see the collect pass in
561			// RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF for why we never scope to a single shard.
562			newTree, err = rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction(repo, tree, "", redactedByPath)
563			if err != nil {
564				return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
565			}
566		}
567	
568		parents := []plumbing.Hash{}
569		if !parent.IsZero() {
570			parents = append(parents, parent)
571		}
572		c := &object.Commit{
573			Author:       oldCommit.Author,
574			Committer:    oldCommit.Committer,
575			Message:      trailers.AppendOPFAppliedTrailer(oldCommit.Message),
576			TreeHash:     newTree,
577			ParentHashes: parents,
578		}
579		// Sign the rewritten commit when commit signing is enabled, matching
580		// every other commit-construction site in this package (common.go,
581		// metadata_reconcile.go, push_common.go). Without this, a user who
582		// has signed checkpoint commits would see the rewrite produce
583		// unsigned commits — silently degrading their integrity story.
584		checkpoint.SignCommitBestEffort(ctx, c)
585		obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
586		if err := c.Encode(obj); err != nil {
587			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode commit: %w", err)
588		}
589		hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
590		if err != nil {
591			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store commit: %w", err)
592		}
593		return hash, nil
594	}

596	// isRedactableBlobName reports whether a file at the given name should
597	// flow through OPF. The policy is fail-closed: every regular file
598	// inside the shard is redacted EXCEPT content_hash.txt, which is
599	// recomputed against the new full.jsonl in a deferred pass.
600	//
601	// Why an open policy: a closed allowlist (.jsonl/.txt/.json only)
602	// would silently skip any future blob type that lands in a shard
603	// — .md prose, agent dumps, no-extension transcript blobs — and ship
604	// it verbatim with the Entire-OPF-Applied trailer attached. Inverting
605	// to "redact everything except the deferred file" means new types are
606	// covered by default; opting out requires an explicit code change.
607	//
608	// The batch redactor (redact.BatchBytesWithPrivacyFilter, via
609	// NamedBlob) handles arbitrary content: .jsonl/.json go through
610	// JSON-aware leaf redaction; anything else gets byte redaction over
611	// the raw content. The OPF has-space gate excludes binary blobs from
612	// paying inference cost.
613	func isRedactableBlobName(name string) bool {
614		return name != paths.ContentHashFileName
615	}

617	// collectTreeBlobs walks the whole tree and appends every redactable
618	// blob's content + full tree path to the parallel output slices. It
619	// walks the entire tree (no shard scoping — see RewriteUnpushedV1WithOPF
620	// for why); rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction applies the same walk so the
621	// cached keys line up.
622	//
623	// blobs[i] and paths[i] correspond: paths[i] is the full path within
624	// the tree (e.g. "ab/cd.../0/full.jsonl"), used later by the apply
625	// walker to find each blob's redacted bytes in the cached map.
626	func collectTreeBlobs(repo *git.Repository, tree *object.Tree, pathPrefix string, blobs *[]redact.NamedBlob, paths *[]string) error {
627		for _, e := range tree.Entries {
628			switch e.Mode {
629			case filemode.Dir:
630				// Externalized image assets are opaque binary lifted out of the
631				// (already redaction-skipped) transcript; byte-redacting them would
632				// only corrupt the images. Skip the whole subtree — symmetrically with
633				// rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction, which preserves it verbatim.
634				if e.Name == assetsDirName {
635					continue
636				}
637				subPath := e.Name
638				if pathPrefix != "" {
639					subPath = pathPrefix + "/" + e.Name
640				}
641				subTree, err := repo.TreeObject(e.Hash)
642				if err != nil {
643					return fmt.Errorf("load subtree %s/%s: %w", pathPrefix, e.Name, err)
644				}
645				if err := collectTreeBlobs(repo, subTree, subPath, blobs, paths); err != nil {
646					return err
647				}
648			case filemode.Regular, filemode.Executable:
649				if !isRedactableBlobName(e.Name) {
650					continue
651				}
652				content, err := readBlob(repo, e.Hash)
653				if err != nil {
654					return fmt.Errorf("read blob %s/%s: %w", pathPrefix, e.Name, err)
655				}
656				fullPath := e.Name
657				if pathPrefix != "" {
658					fullPath = pathPrefix + "/" + e.Name
659				}
660				*blobs = append(*blobs, redact.NamedBlob{Name: e.Name, Content: content})
661				*paths = append(*paths, fullPath)
662			case filemode.Empty, filemode.Deprecated, filemode.Symlink, filemode.Submodule:
663				// Non-blob/non-tree entries are not redactable blobs.
664			}
665		}
666		return nil
667	}

669	// rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction walks the whole tree and produces a new
670	// tree using the precomputed redactedByPath map for redactable blobs.
671	// content_hash.txt files are recomputed in a second pass against the
672	// new full.jsonl in the same directory.
673	//
674	// Path-specific behavior:
675	//   - content_hash.txt → SHA256 of the sibling full.jsonl's new bytes
676	//     (deferred; not redacted itself)
677	//   - everything else → bytes looked up in redactedByPath. The
678	//     fail-closed policy redacts ANY regular file except content_hash.txt,
679	//     not just a closed allowlist of suffixes — a future blob type
680	//     (.md prose, agent dumps, no-extension transcript blobs) is
681	//     covered by default rather than slipping through. The collect
682	//     pass (collectTreeBlobs) populated redactedByPath using the same
683	//     "everything except content_hash.txt" predicate so the keys
684	//     match.
685	//
686	// A redactable blob missing from redactedByPath is either a
687	// programmer error (collect-pass / apply-pass walks went out of sync)
688	// OR a concurrent storage mutation that changed the tree between
689	// passes; we abort the rewrite rather than silently shipping
690	// unredacted content with the OPF-applied trailer.
691	func rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction(repo *git.Repository, tree *object.Tree, pathPrefix string, redactedByPath map[string][]byte) (plumbing.Hash, error) {
692		entries := make([]object.TreeEntry, 0, len(tree.Entries))
693		// deferredHashes records indexes of content_hash.txt entries we
694		// need to recompute after the full.jsonl in the same dir is built.
695		type deferred struct {
696			idx       int
697			entryName string
698			entryMode filemode.FileMode
699		}
700		var deferredHashes []deferred
701		var newFullJSONLHash plumbing.Hash
702	
703		for _, e := range tree.Entries {
704			switch e.Mode {
705			case filemode.Dir:
706				// Preserve externalized image assets verbatim (see collectTreeBlobs):
707				// they are opaque binary and carry no redactable text. Copying the
708				// subtree hash keeps blobs byte-identical so restore still round-trips.
709				if e.Name == assetsDirName {
710					entries = append(entries, e)
711					continue
712				}
713				subPath := e.Name
714				if pathPrefix != "" {
715					subPath = pathPrefix + "/" + e.Name
716				}
717				subTree, err := repo.TreeObject(e.Hash)
718				if err != nil {
719					return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("load subtree %s/%s: %w", pathPrefix, e.Name, err)
720				}
721				newSub, err := rebuildTreeWithCachedRedaction(repo, subTree, subPath, redactedByPath)
722				if err != nil {
723					return plumbing.ZeroHash, err
724				}
725				entries = append(entries, object.TreeEntry{Name: e.Name, Mode: e.Mode, Hash: newSub})
726	
727			case filemode.Regular, filemode.Executable:
728				switch e.Name {
729				case paths.ContentHashFileName:
730					deferredHashes = append(deferredHashes, deferred{idx: len(entries), entryName: e.Name, entryMode: e.Mode})
731					entries = append(entries, e) // placeholder; fixed in second pass
732				default:
733					// Inverted policy: every regular file except
734					// content_hash.txt expects redacted bytes from the
735					// collect pass. A missing key means the collect pass
736					// didn't visit this path — either the storage changed
737					// between passes or the two walkers disagree on which
738					// files to include. Fail-closed.
739					fullPath := e.Name
740					if pathPrefix != "" {
741						fullPath = pathPrefix + "/" + e.Name
742					}
743					newBytes, ok := redactedByPath[fullPath]
744					if !ok {
745						return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("redacted bytes missing for %s "+
746							"(collect/apply walk drift or concurrent storage mutation)", fullPath)
747					}
748					newHash, err := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, newBytes)
749					if err != nil {
750						return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("write redacted blob %s: %w", fullPath, err)
751					}
752					entries = append(entries, object.TreeEntry{Name: e.Name, Mode: e.Mode, Hash: newHash})
753					if e.Name == paths.TranscriptFileName {
754						newFullJSONLHash = newHash
755					}
756				}
757			case filemode.Empty, filemode.Deprecated, filemode.Symlink, filemode.Submodule:
758				entries = append(entries, e)
759			}
760		}
761	
762		for _, d := range deferredHashes {
763			if newFullJSONLHash.IsZero() {
764				continue // no transcript in this dir; keep original hash
765			}
766			jsonlBytes, err := readBlob(repo, newFullJSONLHash)
767			if err != nil {
768				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("read new transcript for content_hash: %w", err)
769			}
770			sum := sha256.Sum256(jsonlBytes)
771			hashBlob, err := checkpoint.CreateBlobFromContent(repo, []byte(fmt.Sprintf("sha256:%x", sum)))
772			if err != nil {
773				return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("write content_hash: %w", err)
774			}
775			entries[d.idx] = object.TreeEntry{Name: d.entryName, Mode: d.entryMode, Hash: hashBlob}
776		}
777	
778		newTree := &object.Tree{Entries: entries}
779		obj := repo.Storer.NewEncodedObject()
780		if err := newTree.Encode(obj); err != nil {
781			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("encode tree: %w", err)
782		}
783		hash, err := repo.Storer.SetEncodedObject(obj)
784		if err != nil {
785			return plumbing.ZeroHash, fmt.Errorf("store tree: %w", err)
786		}
787		return hash, nil
788	}

790	func readBlob(repo *git.Repository, hash plumbing.Hash) ([]byte, error) {
791		blob, err := repo.BlobObject(hash)
792		if err != nil {
793			return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob: %w", err)
794		}
795		r, err := blob.Reader()
796		if err != nil {
797			return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob reader: %w", err)
798		}
799		defer func() { _ = r.Close() }()
800		data, err := io.ReadAll(r)
801		if err != nil {
802			return nil, fmt.Errorf("blob read: %w", err)
803		}
804		return data, nil
805	}

807	// atomicSetV1Ref CAS-updates the local v1 ref. A concrete
808	// ErrReferenceHasChanged from the storer means another worktree
809	// advanced the ref during our rewrite — return V1RefMovedError so the
810	// hook aborts the push. Other errors (I/O, packed-ref locks, storage
811	// bugs) get wrapped as-is so they aren't misreported as concurrency
812	// failures.
813	func atomicSetV1Ref(repo *git.Repository, expectedOld, newHash plumbing.Hash) error {
814		refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName)
815		err := repo.Storer.CheckAndSetReference(
816			plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, newHash),
817			plumbing.NewHashReference(refName, expectedOld),
818		)
819		if err == nil {
820			return nil
821		}
822		if errors.Is(err, storage.ErrReferenceHasChanged) {
823			actual := plumbing.ZeroHash
824			if cur, refErr := repo.Reference(refName, true); refErr == nil {
825				actual = cur.Hash()
826			}
827			return &V1RefMovedError{Expected: expectedOld, Actual: actual}
828		}
829		return fmt.Errorf("set v1 ref: %w", err)
830	}

1	package checkpoint
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"strings"
6	
7		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing"
8	
9		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/id"
10	)
11	
12	// CheckpointRefPrefix is the namespace under which the git-refs backend stores
13	// one ref per checkpoint: refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>. Each ref points
14	// at a checkpoint commit whose tree root is that checkpoint's contents. This is
15	// distinct from the git-branch backend's single entire/checkpoints/v1 branch.
16	const CheckpointRefPrefix = "refs/entire/checkpoints/"
17	
18	// RefName returns the per-checkpoint git ref for a checkpoint ID:
19	// refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>, where <shard> is id.ShardFor() (the
20	// last two characters of the ID for both legacy hex and ULID formats). The full
21	// ID is always the leaf, so the ref round-trips through ParseRef.
22	//
23	// It errors on an empty or unrecognized checkpoint ID rather than returning a
24	// malformed ref (e.g. "refs/entire/checkpoints//"), so callers at trust
25	// boundaries — and future ones — can't silently push, fetch, or look up a bad
26	// ref.
27	func RefName(cid id.CheckpointID) (plumbing.ReferenceName, error) {
28		if cid.Kind() == id.KindUnknown {
29			return "", fmt.Errorf("cannot build checkpoint ref: invalid checkpoint ID %q", cid)
30		}
31		return plumbing.ReferenceName(CheckpointRefPrefix + cid.ShardFor() + "/" + cid.String()), nil
32	}
33	
34	// ParseRef extracts the checkpoint ID from a per-checkpoint ref name,
35	// reporting whether name is a well-formed checkpoint ref. A ref is well-formed
36	// when it has the CheckpointRefPrefix, exactly a <shard>/<id> tail, and the
37	// shard matches the ID's own ShardFor — so refs the resolver did not write
38	// (mismatched shard, extra path segments) are rejected rather than silently
39	// resolved to the wrong bucket. It does not require the ID to be a recognized
40	// kind, so a future ID format still parses as long as it shards consistently.
41	func ParseRef(name plumbing.ReferenceName) (id.CheckpointID, bool) {
42		s := name.String()
43		tail, ok := strings.CutPrefix(s, CheckpointRefPrefix)
44		if !ok {
45			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
46		}
47		shard, rest, ok := strings.Cut(tail, "/")
48		if !ok || shard == "" || rest == "" {
49			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
50		}
51		// Reject extra path segments: the tail must be exactly <shard>/<id>.
52		if strings.Contains(rest, "/") {
53			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
54		}
55		cid := id.CheckpointID(rest)
56		if cid.ShardFor() != shard {
57			return id.EmptyCheckpointID, false
58		}
59		return cid, true
60	}

25	// partitionLocalRefs splits refs into those that exist locally (pushable) and
26	// those that don't (stale queue entries — e.g. a checkpoint ref deleted by
27	// cleanup). Stale refs can never push, so callers drop them from the queue
28	// rather than retrying them forever.
29	func partitionLocalRefs(repo *git.Repository, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) (existing, stale []plumbing.ReferenceName) {
30		for _, ref := range refs {
31			_, err := repo.Reference(ref, false)
32			switch {
33			case err == nil:
34				existing = append(existing, ref)
35			case errors.Is(err, plumbing.ErrReferenceNotFound):
36				// Genuinely gone (e.g. deleted by cleanup) — never pushable, drop it.
37				stale = append(stale, ref)
38			default:
39				// A transient/IO lookup error: keep the ref as pushable so a real
40				// entry isn't dropped from the queue forever over a flaky read.
41				existing = append(existing, ref)
42			}
43		}
44		return existing, stale
45	}
46	
47	// batchPushRefs pushes all of refs to target in a single git push,
48	// fast-forward-only (NOT a force push). Batching keeps a backfill of many refs to
49	// one network round-trip. Per-checkpoint refs normally advance by fast-forward
50	// (each write parents on the prior tip), so the common case succeeds; a
51	// non-fast-forward update — genuine divergence, e.g. the same checkpoint written
52	// differently on another machine — is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting
53	// the remote. We deliberately do not force: there is no server-side ref
54	// protection, so a force push would make a buggy or racing client clobber good
55	// remote history with no signal. On rejection the whole push errors; the caller
56	// retries the rejected refs individually with fetch+replay recovery
57	// (pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery).
58	func batchPushRefs(ctx context.Context, target string, refs []plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
59		if len(refs) == 0 {
60			return nil
61		}
62		refSpecs := make([]string, 0, len(refs))
63		for _, ref := range refs {
64			refSpecs = append(refSpecs, ref.String()+":"+ref.String())
65		}
66		if _, err := remote.PushWithOptions(ctx, remote.PushOptions{Remote: target, RefSpecs: refSpecs}); err != nil {
67			return fmt.Errorf("push %d checkpoint refs: %w", len(refs), err)
68		}
69		return nil
70	}
71	
72	// pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery pushes a single checkpoint ref fast-forward-only;
73	// on rejection — typically the ref diverged on the remote (the same checkpoint
74	// re-written elsewhere) — it fetches the remote ref and replays the local-only
75	// commits on top via fetchAndRebaseRefCommon, then retries. The retry is still
76	// non-force: after the replay the local ref is a fast-forward over the remote, so
77	// the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor rather than overwritten. The
78	// cherry-pick is delta-based, so non-overlapping changes merge; a genuine overlap
79	// (e.g. both sides rewrote the root metadata.json) surfaces as a rebase error and
80	// the ref is left for a later pre-push. Returns nil only if the ref reached the
81	// remote.
82	func pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) error {
83		// One shared budget across the initial push, fetch+replay, and retry, matching
84		// doPushRef (fetchAndRebaseRefCommon relies on the caller's deadline).
85		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, checkpointPushBudget)
86		defer cancel()
87	
88		if err := batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref}); err == nil {
89			return nil
90		}
91		if err := fetchAndRebaseRefCommon(ctx, target, ref); err != nil {
92			return fmt.Errorf("sync diverged checkpoint ref %s: %w", ref, err)
93		}
94		return batchPushRefs(ctx, target, []plumbing.ReferenceName{ref})
95	}
96	
97	// pushRefIfNeeded pushes a ref to the given target if it has unpushed changes.
98	// The target can be a remote name (e.g., "origin") or a URL for direct push.
99	// For branch refs, the "has unpushed" optimization consults the remote-tracking
100	// ref. Non-branch refs and URL targets skip the optimization and let git
101	// handle the no-op case.
102	// Does not check any settings — callers are responsible for gating.
103	func pushRefIfNeeded(ctx context.Context, target string, ref plumbing.ReferenceName) (delivered bool, err error) {
104		repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
105		if err != nil {
106			logging.Debug(ctx, "push skipped: open repository failed",
107				slog.String("ref", ref.String()),
108				slog.String("error", err.Error()))
109			return false, nil
110		}
111		defer repo.Close()
112	
113		localRef, err := repo.Reference(ref, true)
114		if err != nil {
115			// Ref doesn't exist locally — nothing to push, and nothing delivered.
116			// Reporting false rather than "vacuously delivered" keeps a caller that
117			// gates on delivery from acting on a ref that never existed.
118			return false, nil
119		}
120	
121		if ref.IsBranch() && !remote.IsURL(target) && !hasUnpushedBranchRef(repo, target, localRef.Hash(), ref.Short()) {
122			// Local matches the target's tracking ref: the data is already there,
123			// which is delivery as far as any caller can tell.
124			return true, nil
125		}
126	
127		return doPushRef(ctx, target, ref)
128	}

`.entire/logs/entire.log` and OPF falls back to resolving `opf` on `$PATH`. If
that binary is missing, the pre-push rewrite fails closed rather than pushing
content you believed OPF had scanned. Everything else in the OPF block
(`enabled`, `categories`, `timeout_seconds`, `prompt_default`) is ordinary
configuration and still works from the shared project file.

The interactive prompt offers three options and reacts to **Ctrl-C** for cancellation:

```
Run OpenAI Privacy Filter on these checkpoints?
Adds ~30s but redacts names/PII the regex layers can't catch.
Ctrl-C to cancel the push.

  ▸ Yes — run OPF this push
    No — skip OPF, push as-is
    Always — run OPF on every push from now on
```

- **Yes** runs OPF for this push only.
- **No** skips OPF for this push only; the 8-layer-redacted content reaches the remote.
- **Always** runs OPF this push AND writes `prompt_default: "always"` to `.entire/settings.local.json` so future pushes don't ask.
- **Ctrl-C** aborts the push entirely — `git push` exits non-zero, no refs go to the remote.

Non-interactive contexts (CI, scripted pipes with no TTY) skip the prompt and run OPF automatically when enabled, printing `→ OpenAI Privacy Filter: scanning checkpoints…` to stderr so the wait isn't silent. Set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` to skip OPF in those contexts without disabling the feature globally.

**CI consideration**: if you've enabled OPF locally and your CI runs `git push` (e.g. an agent-driven workflow), the CI push will attempt to run OPF too. If the `opf` binary isn't installed in CI, the push will abort with `OPFRuntimeFailedError` rather than silently shipping under-redacted content — by design, since "I enabled OPF" should mean "no content leaves my machines without OPF." The remedies are (a) install `opf` in CI, (b) set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` for CI pushes, or (c) set `prompt_default: "never"` if you only want OPF on interactive pushes.

OPF failures at push time are **fail-closed**: if OPF is not on PATH, fails to start, or times out during the pre-push rewrite, the per-process circuit breaker trips and no under-redacted content reaches the remote. The intent is that "the user enabled OPF" means "I do not want unredacted content leaving this machine" — falling back to 8-layer silently on the push path would violate that contract. Fix the install or set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` for a one-off push.

How that is enforced depends on the checkpoint backend, because they have different escape hatches:

- **git-branch**: the rewrite aborts the push with `OPF runtime failed; aborting push`. Your `git push` exits non-zero. The checkpoint branch travels with that push, so refusing the push is the only way to withhold it.
- **git-refs**: checkpoint refs are pushed separately from your branch and stay queued when they are not flushed, so the failure withholds the checkpoint push and lets your own `git push` succeed. Nothing under-redacted ships either way. This is not silent: a warning names the failure and states that checkpoint refs stayed queued for the next push.

(The circuit breaker is per-process, so a broken install costs one warning instead of one timeout per blob — but the push still aborts.)

Cost note: each shell-out loads the OPF model (~1.5B parameters on CPU). The pre-push rewrite batches **every redactable leaf across every unpushed commit** — v1 commits on git-branch, every unpushed commit on every queued ref on git-refs — into a single inference pass, so a typical real-world push pays the model-load cost once (~6s) plus inference (~5s per 100KB of leaf content) — not multiplied by the number of commits or blobs. A 3-commit push with ~250KB of total prose content runs in ~12–15s, not the ~50–100s a per-blob flow would take. Per-commit latency is unaffected because OPF doesn't run at commit time.

#### When OPF actually runs

OPF execution lives in the pre-push hook. The flow:

1. **Post-commit** writes the checkpoint with **8-layer-only** redaction to your local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Fast, predictable, no OPF cost on the hot path.
2. **Pre-push** (`git push`): if OPF is enabled, the hook re-reads each unpushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` commit, runs the OpenAI Privacy Filter over its blobs to add the categories the regex layers don't catch (person names, addresses, etc.), and builds **new commits** carrying an `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer. The local v1 ref fast-forwards atomically to the new tip, and the (now 9-layer-redacted) commits are what get pushed.
3. The original 8-layer-only commits become **unreachable** in the local git object database and eventually get swept by `git gc`.

This means:

- **The remote only ever sees 9-layer-redacted content** when OPF is enabled.
- **Local-only commits are 8-layer-redacted** until the moment you push. If you never push, OPF never runs.
- **Re-running pre-push is idempotent** — commits already carrying the trailer get re-parented into the chain but are not re-redacted.

#### Force-pushed remote, bootstrap, and concurrent pushes

The rewrite refuses to proceed and aborts the push when it detects a divergent state, so checkpoints on the remote are never silently rebased:

- **Diverged remote**: if local `entire/checkpoints/v1` has commits that aren't ancestors of `<remote>/entire/checkpoints/v1`, the hook exits with a `entire/checkpoints/v1 has diverged from remote` error. Fetch the remote and either reset local v1 to the remote tip or resolve manually before pushing.
- **Bootstrap** (remote has no `entire/checkpoints/v1` yet, e.g. first push): the cap is `100` unpushed commits by default. Override via the env var on the push invocation:

  ```fish
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT 500; git push
  # or fully unbounded:
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT unlimited; git push
  ```

- **Batch-size cap**: independent of commit count, the rewrite refuses pushes whose cumulative prose-leaf content exceeds `ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT` bytes (default: 2 MiB ≈ ~110s of inference). The two caps protect different failure modes — the bootstrap cap stops "100 throwaway commits", the batch cap stops "one commit with 50 MB of pasted transcript". An `OPF would run inference on …` error means you've hit this; bump the env var or push without OPF for that push:

  ```fish
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT 10485760; git push   # 10 MiB
  # or fully unbounded:
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT unlimited; git push
  ```

- **Concurrent push** from another worktree: the rewrite uses a CAS to update the local v1 ref. If another process moved the ref while OPF was running, the hook exits with a "concurrent push detected" error and `git push` aborts the whole batch. Fetch and retry.

#### Persistence of un-redacted-by-OPF content

Three places retain content that OPF *didn't* redact, with different lifetimes. Understanding them matters if your threat model goes beyond "what reaches the remote":

| Location | Redaction level | Lifetime | Reaches remote? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` | **None — raw** | Until the session's data is cleaned up (`entire clean`) | No |
| The agent's own transcript (e.g. `~/.claude/projects/…`) | **None — raw** | Owned and managed by the agent | No |
| Shadow branch `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` | 8-layer | Auto-deleted after the next successful push (only when its session has ended cleanly) | No |
| Unreachable git objects after pre-push rewrite | 8-layer | Until `git gc --prune` (default `gc.pruneExpire` is 2 weeks) | No |
| Reflog `git reflog show entire/checkpoints/v1` | 8-layer tips | Default `gc.reflogExpire` is 90 days | No |
| `<remote>/entire/checkpoints/v1` | 9-layer (after OPF rewrite) | Until you delete the branch on the remote | Yes |

`.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is Entire's own local working copy of the transcript, written mode `0600`. It is *sanitized* (agent state that cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint is stripped) but **not redacted** — redaction happens on the way into a git object, not on this file. It is the input the shadow-branch walk and condensation read from.

The agent's own transcript is never modified at all. Entire reads from it and leaves it alone, because the agent is writing to it continuously and editing under the agent's feet would corrupt the session.

To aggressively scrub the unreachable git objects from the pre-push rewrite (instead of waiting for the 2-week GC window):

```fish
git reflog expire --expire-unreachable=now refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
git gc --prune=now
```

This is I/O-heavy on large repositories; it's not run automatically. If you want it as part of your push workflow, wrap `git push` in a script that invokes it after a successful push.

Verifying it's working:

```fish
# After enabling OPF, run an agent turn that includes a name in the prompt,
# e.g. "Create notes.txt with: Alice Johnson reviewed the proposal."
# Commit (this stays on the fast 8-layer pipeline), then push. OPF runs
# during the pre-push step:
git commit -m "demo"
git push   # → "→ OpenAI Privacy Filter: scanning N checkpoints (~30s)…"
git log --oneline entire/checkpoints/v1 | head -2
entire checkpoint explain HEAD | grep -i 'REDACTED_PERSON'
```

If `[REDACTED_PERSON]` appears in the prompt or transcript section and the latest `entire/checkpoints/v1` commit carries `Entire-OPF-Applied: true`, OPF is active.

```
Adds ~30s but redacts names/PII the regex layers can't catch.
Ctrl-C to cancel the push.

  ▸ Yes — run OPF this push
    No — skip OPF, push as-is
    Always — run OPF on every push from now on
```

- **Yes** runs OPF for this push only.
- **No** skips OPF for this push only; the 8-layer-redacted content reaches the remote.
- **Always** runs OPF this push AND writes `prompt_default: "always"` to `.entire/settings.local.json` so future pushes don't ask.
- **Ctrl-C** aborts the push entirely — `git push` exits non-zero, no refs go to the remote.

Non-interactive contexts (CI, scripted pipes with no TTY) skip the prompt and run OPF automatically when enabled, printing `→ OpenAI Privacy Filter: scanning checkpoints…` to stderr so the wait isn't silent. Set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` to skip OPF in those contexts without disabling the feature globally.

**CI consideration**: if you've enabled OPF locally and your CI runs `git push` (e.g. an agent-driven workflow), the CI push will attempt to run OPF too. If the `opf` binary isn't installed in CI, the push will abort with `OPFRuntimeFailedError` rather than silently shipping under-redacted content — by design, since "I enabled OPF" should mean "no content leaves my machines without OPF." The remedies are (a) install `opf` in CI, (b) set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` for CI pushes, or (c) set `prompt_default: "never"` if you only want OPF on interactive pushes.

OPF failures at push time are **fail-closed**: if OPF is not on PATH, fails to start, or times out during the pre-push rewrite, the per-process circuit breaker trips and no under-redacted content reaches the remote. The intent is that "the user enabled OPF" means "I do not want unredacted content leaving this machine" — falling back to 8-layer silently on the push path would violate that contract. Fix the install or set `ENTIRE_OPF=no` for a one-off push.

How that is enforced depends on the checkpoint backend, because they have different escape hatches:

- **git-branch**: the rewrite aborts the push with `OPF runtime failed; aborting push`. Your `git push` exits non-zero. The checkpoint branch travels with that push, so refusing the push is the only way to withhold it.
- **git-refs**: checkpoint refs are pushed separately from your branch and stay queued when they are not flushed, so the failure withholds the checkpoint push and lets your own `git push` succeed. Nothing under-redacted ships either way. This is not silent: a warning names the failure and states that checkpoint refs stayed queued for the next push.

(The circuit breaker is per-process, so a broken install costs one warning instead of one timeout per blob — but the push still aborts.)

Cost note: each shell-out loads the OPF model (~1.5B parameters on CPU). The pre-push rewrite batches **every redactable leaf across every unpushed commit** — v1 commits on git-branch, every unpushed commit on every queued ref on git-refs — into a single inference pass, so a typical real-world push pays the model-load cost once (~6s) plus inference (~5s per 100KB of leaf content) — not multiplied by the number of commits or blobs. A 3-commit push with ~250KB of total prose content runs in ~12–15s, not the ~50–100s a per-blob flow would take. Per-commit latency is unaffected because OPF doesn't run at commit time.

#### When OPF actually runs

OPF execution lives in the pre-push hook. The flow:

1. **Post-commit** writes the checkpoint with **8-layer-only** redaction to your local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. Fast, predictable, no OPF cost on the hot path.
2. **Pre-push** (`git push`): if OPF is enabled, the hook re-reads each unpushed `entire/checkpoints/v1` commit, runs the OpenAI Privacy Filter over its blobs to add the categories the regex layers don't catch (person names, addresses, etc.), and builds **new commits** carrying an `Entire-OPF-Applied: true` trailer. The local v1 ref fast-forwards atomically to the new tip, and the (now 9-layer-redacted) commits are what get pushed.
3. The original 8-layer-only commits become **unreachable** in the local git object database and eventually get swept by `git gc`.

This means:

- **The remote only ever sees 9-layer-redacted content** when OPF is enabled.
- **Local-only commits are 8-layer-redacted** until the moment you push. If you never push, OPF never runs.
- **Re-running pre-push is idempotent** — commits already carrying the trailer get re-parented into the chain but are not re-redacted.

#### Force-pushed remote, bootstrap, and concurrent pushes

The rewrite refuses to proceed and aborts the push when it detects a divergent state, so checkpoints on the remote are never silently rebased:

- **Diverged remote**: if local `entire/checkpoints/v1` has commits that aren't ancestors of `<remote>/entire/checkpoints/v1`, the hook exits with a `entire/checkpoints/v1 has diverged from remote` error. Fetch the remote and either reset local v1 to the remote tip or resolve manually before pushing.
- **Bootstrap** (remote has no `entire/checkpoints/v1` yet, e.g. first push): the cap is `100` unpushed commits by default. Override via the env var on the push invocation:

  ```fish
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT 500; git push
  # or fully unbounded:
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BOOTSTRAP_LIMIT unlimited; git push
  ```

- **Batch-size cap**: independent of commit count, the rewrite refuses pushes whose cumulative prose-leaf content exceeds `ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT` bytes (default: 2 MiB ≈ ~110s of inference). The two caps protect different failure modes — the bootstrap cap stops "100 throwaway commits", the batch cap stops "one commit with 50 MB of pasted transcript". An `OPF would run inference on …` error means you've hit this; bump the env var or push without OPF for that push:

  ```fish
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT 10485760; git push   # 10 MiB
  # or fully unbounded:
  set -x ENTIRE_OPF_BATCH_LIMIT unlimited; git push
  ```

- **Concurrent push** from another worktree: the rewrite uses a CAS to update the local v1 ref. If another process moved the ref while OPF was running, the hook exits with a "concurrent push detected" error and `git push` aborts the whole batch. Fetch and retry.

#### Persistence of un-redacted-by-OPF content

Three places retain content that OPF *didn't* redact, with different lifetimes. Understanding them matters if your threat model goes beyond "what reaches the remote":

| Location | Redaction level | Lifetime | Reaches remote? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` | **None — raw** | Until the session's data is cleaned up (`entire clean`) | No |
| The agent's own transcript (e.g. `~/.claude/projects/…`) | **None — raw** | Owned and managed by the agent | No |
| Shadow branch `entire/<commit>-<worktree>` | 8-layer | Auto-deleted after the next successful push (only when its session has ended cleanly) | No |
| Unreachable git objects after pre-push rewrite | 8-layer | Until `git gc --prune` (default `gc.pruneExpire` is 2 weeks) | No |
| Reflog `git reflog show entire/checkpoints/v1` | 8-layer tips | Default `gc.reflogExpire` is 90 days | No |
| `<remote>/entire/checkpoints/v1` | 9-layer (after OPF rewrite) | Until you delete the branch on the remote | Yes |

`.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is Entire's own local working copy of the transcript, written mode `0600`. It is *sanitized* (agent state that cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint is stripped) but **not redacted** — redaction happens on the way into a git object, not on this file. It is the input the shadow-branch walk and condensation read from.

The agent's own transcript is never modified at all. Entire reads from it and leaves it alone, because the agent is writing to it continuously and editing under the agent's feet would corrupt the session.

To aggressively scrub the unreachable git objects from the pre-push rewrite (instead of waiting for the 2-week GC window):

```fish
git reflog expire --expire-unreachable=now refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1
git gc --prune=now
```

This is I/O-heavy on large repositories; it's not run automatically. If you want it as part of your push workflow, wrap `git push` in a script that invokes it after a successful push.

git-refs: `runOPFForCheckpointRefs` returns `false` on any failure and `prePushCheckpointRefs` does `return nil` (`manual_commit_push.go:399-401`), so **the user's push proceeds**; refs stay queued because Peek (not Drain) was used and `flushCheckpointRefsQueue` never runs. A warning goes to both the log and `stderrWriter` (`manual_commit_push.go:268-274`). Verified by `TestPrePushCheckpointRefs_OPFFailureWithholdsFlush` (`manual_commit_opf_rewrite_test.go:973-993`), which asserts `PrePushFromGitHook` returns nil, refs stay queued, and `ls-remote` shows nothing.

## 3. Ref update semantics

- git-branch: single CAS on `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` (`rewrite.go:407`, `atomicSetV1Ref` `:813-830`).
- git-refs: **yes, each ref is rewritten in place** — same ref name, new tip, CAS'd with the expected old hash (`refs.go:168-175`, `repo.Storer.CheckAndSetReference`).
- **The push is still fast-forward-only / non-force.** Refspec is `ref:ref` with no leading `+` (`push_common.go:62-66`), and the doc comment at `push_common.go:47-57` is explicit: "fast-forward-only (NOT a force push)… a non-fast-forward update is REJECTED rather than silently overwriting the remote. We deliberately do not force." Recovery retry is also non-force (`push_common.go:76-78`).
- Why the rewrite doesn't break fast-forward: the new chain is parented on `base`, which is the already-pushed trailered commit, so the new tip is still a descendant of the remote tip. Locally the ref move is *not* a fast-forward (old commits become unreachable) — same as v1.

## 5. The `Entire-OPF-Applied` trailer

- **Written by both halves**, via the shared `rebuildCheckpointCommit` → `trailers.AppendOPFAppliedTrailer` (`rewrite.go:575`; called from `rewrite.go:400` and `refs.go:157`). Key/value defined at `/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/worktree-silver-harbor-a927/cmd/entire/cli/trailers/trailers.go:59,64`; only the literal `true` counts (`HasOPFApplied`, `:262-275`); appending is idempotent (`AppendOPFAppliedTrailer`, `:317-324`).
- **It is the discovery watermark only for git-refs** (`refs.go:192`). On git-branch the watermark is the remote tip; there the trailer is only a per-commit "skip re-redaction, just re-parent" flag (`rewrite.go:341`, `:555`).
- Nothing at commit time writes it — condensation is regex-only by design (`checkpoint/persistent.go:691-692`, `:2518-2520`, `checkpoint/prompts.go:27`).
- Trailer survives the divergence replay path: `cherryPickOnto` preserves the original message (`strategy/metadata_reconcile.go:421` comment, `createCherryPickCommit`).

## 6. Where un-redacted-by-OPF content persists — git-refs equivalents

- **Local per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`** (prefix at `/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/worktree-silver-harbor-a927/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/refs_naming.go:16`): **yes — 8-layer before push, 9-layer after the rewrite.** Written 8-layer by condensation (`refs_store.go:203-213`), rewritten in place to 9-layer at pre-push (`refs.go:168-175`). These refs are **never deleted** after push — post-push cleanup only deletes shadow branches under `refs/heads/entire/...` (`strategy/cleanup.go:226-227`, `DeleteShadowBranchesIfUnchanged`), so the 9-layer content is the durable local state.
- **Unreachable objects**: same as v1 — the pre-rewrite 8-layer commits/trees/blobs become unreachable and wait for `git gc --prune`. Add `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` to the scrub recipe.
- **Reflog: effectively no concern for `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`.** Two reasons: (a) all checkpoint-ref writes go through go-git's storer (`SetReference` / `CheckAndSetReference`) and go-git does not append reflog entries on ref writes — `storage/filesystem/dotgit/dotgit.go:840 SetRef` has no reflog call, and reflog is a separate opt-in `AppendReflog` API; (b) git's own `core.logAllRefUpdates=true` default only auto-logs `refs/heads/*`, `refs/remotes/*`, `refs/notes/*` and `HEAD`, so even the reftable seam (`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/worktree-silver-harbor-a927/cmd/entire/cli/gitrepo/reftable.go:195-238`, which shells out to `git update-ref`) does not create one for `refs/entire/*` unless the user set `logAllRefUpdates=always`. The existing "reflog holds 8-layer v1 tips" row is a git-branch-only row.
- **Push queue file: ref names only, no content.** `entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl` in the git common dir; each line is `{"ref":"refs/entire/checkpoints/…"}` (`checkpoint/pushqueue.go:23-31`, `:69`, `:172`), mode `0600` (`:73`), flock-guarded, deleted when empty (`:163-169`). Nothing redactable in it.
- **Shadow branches**: unchanged and shared by both backends (`cleanupPushedShadowBranches` is called on both paths, `manual_commit_push.go:219` and `:416`), 8-layer metadata + raw code snapshots, never OPF'd.
- **Remote-side**: `<remote>` copy of `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`, 9-layer after rewrite. Note there is **no local remote-tracking copy** — the refspec is `ref:ref` (`push_common.go:64`), so nothing lands under `refs/remotes/`.
- **Two git-refs-specific 8-layer sinks the current table misses:**
  1. **A configured git-branch *mirror*.** Mirrors are write-only and explicitly "never receive ref-level mutations such as cleanup deletes or pre-push OPF re-redaction" (`/Users/soph/.herdr/worktrees/cli/worktree-silver-harbor-a927/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/fanout.go:10-17`). So the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` mirror branch retains 8-layer content indefinitely. It is not pushed by pre-push today (`manual_commit_push.go:108-109`), so it does not reach the remote — but it does have a `refs/heads/` reflog.
  2. **A leftover `entire/checkpoints/v1` from migration.** `MigrateBranchToRefs` (`checkpoint/migrate.go:48-…`) imports from the local v1 branch and never deletes it; the 8-layer branch and its reflog survive. Also, migrated refs' commits carry no OPF trailer (message is `"Import checkpoint %s (migrated from git-branch)"`, `migrate.go:135`), so the first post-migration push re-OPFs every migrated ref — 1 commit per ref keeps the per-ref bootstrap cap happy, but the cumulative 2 MiB leaf cap is the realistic trip point.
- **Transient**: `refs/entire-fetch-tmp/...` from the divergence-recovery fetch (`push_common.go:484`) holds remote content and is removed on success (`:546`). The v1 path's `refs/entire-fetch-tmp/opf-rewrite-v1` is cleaned up in a defer (`rewrite.go:427`, `:462-468`).
- One genuine residual gap for refs: the divergence replay cherry-picks local (OPF-applied) commits onto the *fetched remote tip*, keeping the local commit's trailer (`push_common.go:576-597` → `metadata_reconcile.go:399-430`). If the remote tip was pushed 8-layer by another machine, the resulting merged tree carries that 8-layer content under an OPF-applied trailer, and the next push's walk stops there. No *new* content reaches the remote (it came from there), but it will never be OPF'd.

## 7. Verification recipe for git-refs

`git log --oneline <branch>` cannot show the trailer at all (`--oneline` prints only the subject line) — so the git-branch recipe at line 325 is already broken. Working git-refs equivalents:

```fish
# list your checkpoint refs, newest first
git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --format='%(refname) %(objectname:short)' refs/entire/checkpoints/

# check the trailer on the newest one
git for-each-ref --count=1 --sort=-committerdate --format='%(refname)' refs/entire/checkpoints/ \
  | xargs -I{} git log -1 --format='%H%n%B' {}

# or across all of them at once — %(contents) exposes the trailer block
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short) %(trailers:key=Entire-OPF-Applied)' refs/entire/checkpoints/

# confirm the redaction landed
entire checkpoint list
entire checkpoint explain <checkpoint-id> | grep -i 'REDACTED_PERSON'

# what is still queued (nothing queued == everything flushed)
git for-each-ref refs/entire/checkpoints/ | wc -l
cat "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/entire-checkpoint-push-queue.jsonl"
```

For git-branch the trailer-visible form is `git log -1 --format='%H%n%B' entire/checkpoints/v1` (or `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Entire-OPF-Applied)' -2 entire/checkpoints/v1`), not `--oneline`.
